farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلإِنسَانِ حِينٌ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهْرِ﴾.
Its meaning: there has indeed (قد) come upon man a period of time. "هل" may be a denial (jaḥd), and it may be a statement (khabar).
This is of the statement kind; because you may say: "Did I not admonish you (فهل وعظتك)? Did I not give you (فهل أعطيتك)?", making him affirm that you did give him and admonish him. The denial is when you say: "And can anyone (وهل يقدر واحد) do the like of this?"
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿لَمْ يَكُن شَيْئاً مَّذْكُوراً﴾.
He means: he was a thing, but he was not something mentioned. That is from the time Allah created him from clay until He breathed the spirit into him.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْشَاجٍ نَّبْتَلِيهِ﴾.
الأمشاج: the mixtures — the man's fluid, the woman's fluid, the blood and the clot. When something of this sort [117/b] is mixed it is called مشيج, as you say خليط (mixed), and ممشوج, as you say مخلوط (mixed).
His saying: ﴿نَّبْتَلِيهِ﴾ — the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: We made him hearing and seeing in order to test him. This is placed earlier while its meaning is later; the meaning is only: We created him and made him hearing and seeing in order to test him.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾.
Also إلى السبيل and للسبيل; all of that is permissible in the speech of the Arabs. He says: We guided him, i.e. We made the way known to him, whether he is grateful or ungrateful. (إما) here may be conditional (jazāʾ), i.e.: whether he is grateful or whether he is ungrateful; or it may be the (إما) found in His saying: ﴿إِما يُعَذِّبُهُمْ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, as though He said: We created him wretched or happy.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَلاَسِلَ وَأَغْلاَلاً﴾.
"سلاسل" was written with an alif, and some of the readers declined it as a triptote (ajrāhā) because of the alif at its end, while some did not. The one who did not decline it said: the Arabs keep the alif in the accusative of what is a diptote (lā yujrā), and when they join it to what follows they drop the alif; and both are correct. Similar to that is His saying: ﴿كانَتْ قَوَارِيراً﴾ (15): the alif was kept in the first because it is the end of a verse, while the other is not [the end of] a verse. So keeping the alif in the first was stronger because of this argument, and that is how I saw it in the codex of ʿAbdullāh; the people of Basra read it so and wrote it so in their codices. The people of Kufa and Medina keep the alif in both of them together, as though they found it strange for one word with one accusative meaning to be written in two different ways. If you wish, you decline both as triptotes; if you wish, you decline neither; and if you wish, you decline the first because of the alif in the writing of the people of Basra and do not decline the second, since it has no alif.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُوراً﴾.
It is said that it is a spring called al-Kāfūr. It may also be that its mixture is like camphor because of the fragrance of its scent, in which case it is not a name. The Arabs [118/a] put the accusative on whichever of these two words they like. Ḥassān said:
كأنَّ خبيئَةً من بيت رأْسٍ * يكونُ مِزاجُها عَسلٌ وماءُ
(As though a hidden [wine] from Bayt Raʾs, whose mixture is honey and water.)
It is clearer in meaning to make the verb [i.e. its accusative predicate] fall on المزاج, even though it is definite; and all is correct. You say: كان سيدَهم أبوك (your father was their chief) and كان سيدُهم أباك. The preferred way is to say: كان سيدَهم أبوك; because "father" is a fixed noun, whereas "chief" is one of the attributes.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَيْناً﴾.
If you wish, you make it follow الكافور as an explicative of it; and if you wish, you put it in the accusative by detachment (qaṭʿ) from the hāʾ in "مزاجها".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِهَا﴾, and "يَشْرَبُهَا".
They are the same in meaning. It is as though يشرب بها means: quenches his thirst with it and slakes it. As for يشربونها, it is clear. Someone recited to me:
شَرِبْنَ بِمَاءِ البحرِ ثمَّ تَرَفَّعتْ * مَتى لُججٍ خُضْرٍ لَهُنَّ نئيجُ
(They drank of the sea's water, then rose up out of green deep waves, with a roaring sound.)
Similar to it is: إنه ليتكلم بكلام حسن, and يتكلم كلاماً حسناً (he speaks with fine speech / he speaks fine speech).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيراً﴾.
Whichever [place] a man of the people of Paradise likes, he makes it gush forth for himself.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُوفُونَ بِٱلنَّذْرِ﴾.
This is one of their attributes in this world; it is as though there is an implied كان in it: they used to fulfil the vow.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْماً كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيراً﴾.
Its trial is far-spreading. The Arabs say: the crack spread (استطار) in the glass flask and the like, and also استطال.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَبُوساً قَمْطَرِيراً﴾.
القمطرير: the severe. One says: يوم قمطرير and يوم قماطر (a severe day). Someone recited to me:
بَنِى عمِّنا، هل تذكُرونَ بَلاءَنا * علَيكُمْ إذا ما كانَ قُمَاطِرُ
(O sons of our uncle, do you remember our good service to you when there was a severe [day]?)

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He [«عز وجلك» in the source — Translator's note: a typo for «عز وجل:»]: ﴿مُّتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا﴾.
It is in the accusative as by detachment (qaṭʿ). If you wish, you make it follow الجنة, as though you said: their reward is a Garden, reclining in it.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلاَلُهَا﴾.
It may be accusative on that [same pattern]: their reward is a Garden, reclining in it, and its shades being near. If you wish, you make الدانية follow المتكئين by way of detachment (qaṭʿ), which may also be nominative on [118/b] resumption (istiʾnāf). So it is permissible like His saying: ﴿وَهَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخاً﴾ and "وشيخٌ". In the reading of Ubayy it is: "ودانٍ عليهم ظلالها", and this is resumptive, in the position of the nominative; and in the reading of ʿAbdullāh: "ودانياً عليهم ظلالها". The masculine and feminine forms of الداني are like His saying: ﴿خَاشِعاً أبْصَارُهم﴾ in one place and ﴿خاشعةً أبصارهم﴾ in another. الدانية may also be accusative on the pattern of the Arabs' saying: عند فلان جاريةٌ جميلةٌ، وشابةً بعدُ طريةً (So-and-so has a beautiful slave-girl, and young still, fresh), interposing praise parenthetically, without intending it to be coordinated with what precedes; it is as though they imply with this wāw a verb by which the accusative comes about, [as] in one of the two readings: "وحوراً عيناً". Someone recited to me:
ويأوى إلى نسوة عاطلاتٍ * وشُعثا مراضيعَ مثل السعالِى
(And he takes refuge with women bare of ornament, and dishevelled ones, nursing mothers, like ghouls.)
with the accusative, i.e.: وشعثا; though the genitive is more common.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلاً﴾.
The people of Paradise pick the fruit standing and sitting, and in every state, with no effort in it.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَاْ﴾.
He says: they had the clarity of glass and the whiteness of silver, so the clarity of glass and the whiteness of silver were combined in them.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدَّرُوهَا﴾.
They measured the cup to the thirst of each one of them, with nothing left over and nothing falling short of quenching his thirst; and that is the most delightful drink.
Some have transmitted from al-Shaʿbī: (قُدِّروها تَقْدِيراً). The meaning is the same, and Allah knows best: "it was measured for them" and "they measured it" are equivalent.

farraa:17-18.t:
His saying: ﴿كَأْساً كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلاً﴾.
It is only called a كأس when there is drink in it; when there is no wine in it, the name كأس does not apply to it.
I heard one of the Arabs say of the tray on which a gift is presented: it is the مِهْدَى, as long as the gift is on it; when it is [119/a] empty it reverts to its own name, whether it is a tray (طبق) or a table (خوان) or something else.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿زَنجَبِيلاً عَيْناً﴾.
It is mentioned that the ginger (الزنجبيل) is the spring, and that الزنجبيل is a name for it; and the same interpretation applies to it as to الكافور.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تُسَمَّىٰ سَلْسَبِيلاً﴾.
They mentioned that السلسبيل is a name for the spring, and it is mentioned that it is a description of the water for its smooth flowing and its sweetness. We consider that if it were a name for the spring, leaving it undeclined (tark al-ijrāʾ, i.e. treating it as a diptote) would be more common; yet we have not seen any of the readers leave it undeclined, though that is permissible in Arabic, just as in the reading of ʿAbdullāh: ﴿وَلاَ تَذَرُنّ وَدًّا ولا سُوَاعاً ولا يَغُوثاً ويَعُوقاً﴾ with the alif, and as they said "سلاسلا" and "قواريرا" with the alif, declining as triptotes what is not declined. That is not a mistake, because the Arabs decline as triptotes in poetry what is not declined; if it were a mistake they would not have brought it into their poems. Mutammim ibn Nuwayra said:
فما وجد أظآرٍ ثلاثٍ روائمٍ * رأين مَجَرًّا من حُوارٍ ومصْرعَا
(The grief of three foster she-camels, tenderly attached, that saw where a young camel was dragged and where it fell, is not [like mine].)
So he declined روائم as a triptote, though it is one of those not declined — [this occurs] in more instances than I can count in their poems.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُّخَلَّدُونَ﴾.
He says: adorned and wearing bracelets; it is also said: wearing earrings; and it is said: مخلدون means their youth is everlasting, they do not change from that age. This is the most likely to be correct — and Allah knows best — because when a man grows old among the Arabs and the blackness of his hair remains, it is said: إنه لمخلد. Likewise, when he grows old and his teeth and molars remain [firm], it is said: إنه لمخلد, i.e. of unchanging condition.
Likewise the youths: their teeth remain [unchanged].

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيماً﴾.
It is said: when you see what is there (ما ثَمّ), you see bliss; and implying (ما) is acceptable, just as it was said: ﴿لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾, the meaning being: what is between you, and Allah knows best. It is also said: إذا رأيت [119/b] ثم, meaning: when you look; then when you cast your sight there you see bliss.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُندُسٍ﴾.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read it in the accusative, treating it like an adverb: "above them". The Arabs say: قومك داخلَ الدار (your people are inside the house), putting داخل الدار in the accusative because it is a place (maḥall); and عاليهم is of that kind. The people of the Hijaz and Ḥamza read: "عَالِيهم" with the yāʾ left unvowelled (irsāl), and in the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is: "عاليتُهم ثيابُ سُنْدُسٍ" with tāʾ — and that is an argument for whoever leaves the yāʾ unvowelled and makes it quiescent. The readers differed over الخضر and السندس [Translator's note: so in the source; the context indicates خضر and إستبرق]: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb put them both in the genitive, intending to make الخضر a description of السندس and ويكسر على الاستبرق [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently "and to make الاستبرق coordinate with it"] — ثيابُ سندس and ثيابُ استبرق. Al-Ḥasan put both words in the nominative, making الخضر a description of الثياب and putting الاستبرق in the nominative by coordinating it back onto الثياب. Some put الخضر in the nominative and الاستبرق in the genitive, and [others] put الاستبرق in the nominative and الخضر in the genitive; and all of that is correct. And Allah is praised.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿شَرَاباً طَهُوراً﴾.
He says: pure, not impure, as it [wine] was spoken of as impure in this world.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِماً أَوْ كَفُوراً ﴾.
(وُ) [Translator's note: so in the source; read (أو)] here is equivalent to (لا). أو, in denial, interrogation and conditional (jazāʾ) [contexts], has the meaning of (لا), and this is one of those. The poet said:
لا وَجْدُ ثَكْلَى كما وَجِدْتُ وَلا * وَجْدُ عَجُولٍ أَضَلَّهَا رُبَعُ
أَوْ وَجْدُ شيخٍ أصَلَّ ناقَتهُ * يَوْمَ توافَى الحجيجُ فاندفعُوا
(Neither the grief of a bereaved mother is like the grief I felt, nor the grief of a she-camel that lost her young calf, or the grief of an old man who lost his she-camel on the day the pilgrims gathered and then pushed on.)
He meant: ولا وجد شيخ (nor the grief of an old man). In Arabic it may also be: do not obey among them anyone who sins or disbelieves.
Then the meaning of (أو) is close to the meaning of (الواو), as when you say to a man: لأعطينك سألت أو سكتّ (I will surely give to you, whether you ask or keep silent), meaning: I will surely give to you in any case.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying [120/a], Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَشَدَدْنَآ أَسْرَهُمْ﴾.
الأسر: the make (الخلق). You say: لقد أُسِر هذا الرجل أحسنَ الأسر (this man has been made with the finest make), as you say: خُلِقَ أحسنَ الخَلْق (he was created with the finest creation).

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾.
He says: this sura is a reminder and an admonition. ﴿فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً﴾: a direction and a road to good.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ﴾.
A response to His saying: ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتّخذَ إلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Then He informed them that the matter is not up to them, and said: ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ﴾ that way ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ for you. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh: ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, identical to the standard reading; the following remark suggests ʿAbdullāh's reading had (ما) in place of (أن), i.e. «إلا ما شاء الله»]. The meaning of (ما) and (أن) is close.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ﴾.
You put الظالمين in the accusative because the wāw in لها [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently "the lām in لهم" is meant] becomes like an adverbial container (ẓarf) for أعدّ. If it were nominative it would be correct, as He said: ﴿والشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغَاوُونَ﴾ without hamza. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is: "وللظالمين أعد لهم", repeating the lām in (الظالمين) and in (لهم); and the Arabs sometimes do that. Someone recited to me:
أقول لها إذا سألت طلاقا * إلامَ تسارعين إلى فراقى
(I say to her, when she asks for divorce: to what end do you hasten to part from me?)
And someone recited to me:
فأصبحْنَ لا يَسلنهُ عن بما به * أصعَّد فى غاوى الهَوى أم تصوَّبا؟
(And by morning they would not ask him about what was with him: had he gone up in the error of passion, or come down?)
So he repeated the bāʾ twice [Translator's note: in the verse what is repeated is the preposition عن with ب]. Had he said: لا يسلنه عما به, it would have been clearer and better; but the poet sometimes adds and omits to complete the verse. If you directed the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ، عن النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيم﴾ to this interpretation, it would be correct in Arabic.
It has another interpretation, meaning: About what are they asking one another, O Muhammad! Then He informed and said: they are asking one another about the great news. Similar to this is His saying in al-Mursalāt: ﴿لأَِىِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ﴾ as an expression of wonder, then He said: ﴿ليوم الفصل﴾, i.e.: they were deferred to the Day of Decision.
